Subject: Interview grid + debrief protocol for Inference Platform Lead

Hi all,

Zoe Lin (Nate from TalentBridge looped) is scheduled to interview for the Inference Platform Lead role. I attached a first pass rubric and a question grid — please review and propose any changes by EOD Tuesday. Key asks: 

- Confirm who will cover each focus area (system design, model quality/metrics, infra/ops, leadership / team fit).
- Agree on a single scoring anchor (1-4) and the go/no-go threshold. My recommendation: no candidate with avg < 2.5 moves forward without exec review.
- Decide whether we want a short take-home design prompt or rely on live design + code walkthrough.

Logistics: Nate has proposed panel dates June 24-25 (candidate in PDT). If you're unavailable, flag your constraints and a preferred backup.

Attachments: inference-lead-rubric-v1.docx, panel-question-grid.xlsx

Thanks — Markus

On Sun, Jun 20, 2027 at 9:12 AM Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi all,
> 
> Zoe Lin (Nate from TalentBridge looped) is scheduled to interview for the Inference Platform Lead role...

Thanks Markus — quick thoughts after skimming the rubric:

- I'm happy to take ML/metrics + evaluation section. I suggest we add a concrete question set for "tradeoffs in productionizing new model variants" (2-3 bullets) so interviewers can probe decisions rather than surface-level answers.
- For scoring anchors: propose these labels to map to our 1-4 scale: 4 = clearly exceeds (quant evidence), 3 = solid (practical depth), 2 = borderline (missing key tradeoffs), 1 = fail (unsafe or unable to reason).
- On the take-home: I'd skip a formal take-home for this senior hire; prefer a 20-25m focused system design with a 10m follow-up on tradeoffs. If we want a technical artifact, ask for a short writeup post-interview.

I attached a quick note in the rubric (inference-lead-rubric-v1.docx) with inline examples. I'm available both June 24 and 25 afternoon PDT.

- Lauren

Subject: Re: Interview grid + debrief protocol for Inference Platform Lead

Thanks team — I've drafted a short debrief protocol and attached the panel-question-grid.xlsx with specific prompts per interviewer. Notes below: 

- Scoring: use 1-4 numeric scale, then map to recommendation: 3.5-4 = Strong Hire, 3.0-3.4 = Hire, 2.5-2.9 = Consider with follow-up, <2.5 = No.
- Debrief flow: (1) Silent scoring (everyone enters scores in Greenhouse), (2) Short clarifying Qs (panel asks 5m), (3) Discussion & anchor-based calibration (5-10m), (4) Final recommendation.
- Interview anchors: I've included 1-2 anchor bullets per area (system design, model quality, infra ops, leadership). Use those verbatim to reduce variability.
- Time budget: 20m system design, 15m scalability deep-dive, 15m ML/metrics, 10m leadership / culture fit, 5m buffer.

I'll take the system-design slot and own the calendar invites if everyone confirms availability. Also added the Greenhouse eval link and template in attachments (greenhouse-eval-template.pdf).

Attachments: panel-question-grid.xlsx, greenhouse-eval-template.pdf

- Marissa

Thanks everyone — solid alignment. Quick recap and next steps: 

- Roles: Marissa = system design lead; Lauren = ML/metrics & evaluation; Aditya = bar-raiser (reliability/ops); Vivek = infra/ops coverage and follow-up on infra questions.
- Format: 20m live design (Marissa), 15m scalability deep-dive (Aditya), 15m ML/metrics (Lauren), 10m leadership + culture (open). 5m buffer.
- Scoring: 1-4 scale, blind scores in Greenhouse, then 10m discussion. Go/no-go threshold set at avg >= 2.5 for advancement.
- Logistics: Marissa to send calendar invites (please accept or propose swaps). Nate: candidate confirmed for June 24, 2pm PDT. Zoe: please review the short rubric we shared; we will not require a take-home pre-work.

Links & attachments: Greenhouse req (https://greenhouse.example.com/boards/req12345), calendar invite (https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=abc123), rubric in Drive (https://drive.google.com/open?id=1XyzRubric).
